newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures post new high close.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures post new high close.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures powered to a new all-time high settlement in September S&Ps following a late rally triggered by the Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates unchanged.
The Federal Open Market Committee voted to leave short-term rates steady, making its decision known in the early afternoon.

Treasury bond futures responded with a slight tilt upward, notching a new session high in the September contract as it headed into the close. The Fed's decision to leave rates alone was widely anticipated and factored into prices, traders said.

After bonds closed, stock index futures unleashed a furious rally. September S&Ps raced to a new all-time settlement high of 915.50, ending just below the session high of 916.00, which was also a record high.
The contract surpassed the previous all-time high of 912.40 set June 20.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 73 points to 7795, one point off its all-time high.
"It's a friendly environment for stocks," said one S&P stock index trader. "Growth plus no inflation is good for equities."
Early in the session, stocks and bonds were underpinned by the release of weaker than expected U.S. factory orders for May.
May factory orders were reported down 0.7 percent, below analysts' expectations for a 0.2 percent decline. In April, orders were revised upward to a 1.4 percent gain.

The market will now turn its attention to June U.S. employment data, set for release Thursday instead of the usual Friday reporting date due to the July 4 holiday. Thursday will be a shortened trading session for stock index futures.
Nonfarm payrolls are seen rising 222,000, compared with a gain of 138,000 in May, and the unemployment rate is seen unchanged at 4.8 percent.

Sept S&Ps ended 14.25 higher at 915.50, NYSE New Composites up 6.20 at 477.05, Nikkeis up 75 at 20,360, Midcap 400s up 1.60 at 294.35, Nasdaq 100s up 21.80 at 989.25 and Russell 2000s up 1.60 at 399.50. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
